correctness.rationale: Definition 4.1 gives the exact recurrence with A_t the possible-p worlds. A_t is monotone under edge addition; if A_t does not grow, every row at the next stage meets N_t (or N_t is empty), so no later update is strict. Cardinality accounting including initially empty A_0 and empty P proves no more than n strict updates. An explicit n-vertex directed path with p true only at its initial vertex makes precisely one new row eligible per update and first stabilizes after n. Exhaustive relation-and-valuation enumeration for all n<=4 (1,052,740 instances) and the n<=24 path checks corroborate the proof, but the theorem is based on the symbolic argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general dynamic reduction axioms do not assert an iteration cutoff. The idempotence theorem has a strictly narrower (propositional-content) hypothesis and is contradicted if naively extended to modal possibility. The n-state deletion theorem is about another transformation and cannot imply the present sharpness examples.

value.rationale: Sharp stabilization depth is motivated by iterative dynamic belief change and by the contrasting one-step propositional idempotence theorem. The modal formula possibility(p) is a minimal non-propositional test: it yields unbounded iteration depth over growing finite carriers, but a sharp linear n cutoff instead of the naive n^2 edge budget. The directed path is a natural complete sharpness classification of the worst-case scale, relevant to finite dynamic model evaluation.
